Pay varies greatly depending on the job. Hours are long and you'll generally work at 6 days a week. I got the job by applying and being qualified for the position. Every job that is required in a small town is required there, plus scientific research opportunities and grants for short term research. Keep in mind that many people want to go down there. When I was there, for example, a lawyer was working as a janitor, but she also had experience cleaning toilets in a job that helped fund her college, I guess. The dark slows everything down, but work must continue. People become more antisocial in winter. You get used to the dark in winter just as you do 24 sun in summer. Summer brings insomnia for many. The people that go down there are generally very talented and creative, and we share our interests and hobbies with classes and lectures and get togethers. There is also typical internet and movies for entertainment. Hiking and cross country skiing are popular during good weather.
